heroSub: 10 hand-picked Pattaya hotels and resorts that work for a trip with kids, and that we've reviewed in depth — from beachfront resorts with in-house water parks, kids' clubs and bunk-bed family rooms, to kids' pools and water slides, down to serviced apartments with kitchens on a lighter budget. Prices start at about ฿900–6,500/night.
introH2: 👨‍👩‍👧‍👦 Why Pattaya works for families, and how to pick the right stay for your kids
introHtml: Pattaya is one of the easiest beach cities in Thailand to bring the family to. The simple reason is that it's only about a 2-hour drive from Bangkok, and the area is packed with things for kids to do — big water parks like Ramayana Water Park and Columbia Pictures Aquaverse, the Nong Nooch botanical garden, Underwater World, the Sanctuary of Truth, and Khao Kheow Open Zoo not far away. What sets Pattaya's hotels apart from other beach towns is that plenty of resorts have in-house water parks or slide pools and kids' clubs, so children can play all day without going anywhere. But Pattaya's stays come in many kinds — some are designed for couples or nightlife specifically, and book the wrong type and you can end up with a room that's too small or an area that's noisy at night. How to pick the right one for a family: (1) look at room size and type — family rooms, bunk beds, connecting rooms, or kitchen rooms for longer stays; (2) look at the kids' facilities — kids' pool, water park, slides, kids' club; (3) look at the location — quiet private-beach zones (North Pattaya / Pratamnak Hill / Na Jomtien) are for pure relaxation, while central Pattaya is more walkable to malls and attractions. This article gathers 10 Pattaya hotels and resorts that suit families and that we've reviewed in depth — every one drawn from reading real guest reviews, with honest pros and cons, prices compared across 3 sites, and full direct booking links.
mrtHtml: Pattaya has no rail transit; in town people ride songthaews (the red trucks), starting at 10–20 baht per trip, while getting the family out to attractions is easiest by Grab or your own car (most resorts have parking). The areas in this article: North Pattaya / Na Kluea / Wongamat — a quieter, cleaner beach than central Pattaya, near Terminal 21 (Centara Grand Mirage, Dusit Thani). Central Pattaya (Beach Road / Second Road) — the most walkable to the beach, malls and attractions, ideal for families who want to get around easily (Holiday Inn, Somerset, AVANI, The Grass). Pratamnak Hill (South Pattaya) — on a hillside over the bay, with quiet private beaches, 10–15 minutes' drive into town (Royal Cliff, InterContinental). Na Jomtien — a quiet southern zone with private beachfront, close to the big southern water parks (Renaissance, Mövenpick Siam). From U-Tapao Airport (UTP) it's about 30–50 minutes into town, while Suvarnabhumi is about 1.5–2 hours.

entries.type: Luxury 5-Star · Family resort with in-house water park
entries.name: Centara Grand Mirage Beach Resort Pattaya
entries.revCount: Score 9.1 · 2,137 reviews · Lost World theme · Centara group
entries.badge: 🏆 Best family resort with an in-house water park
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Wongamat beach · Na Kluea · 230m private beach · near Terminal 21
entries.storyHtml: If you had to pick one Pattaya resort genuinely built for families with young kids, the reviews hand it to this one most often — Centara Grand Mirage Beach Resort Pattaya is a 555-room, 5-star adventure-themed "Lost World" resort right on Wongamat beach in Na Kluea, north of the centre, where the beach is quieter and cleaner than central Pattaya. It scores 9.1 from 2,137 reviews. What families love most is the in-house Lost World water park — a freeform pool, lazy river, slides, jacuzzis and a shallow Monsoon Island zone for little ones, all playable all day with no entry fee — plus two kids' clubs, and Family Residence rooms and Lost World-themed bunk beds that take several children. There's a private stretch of sand about 230 metres long in front of the resort, and it's close to Terminal 21 mall and Lan Pho market. Honest cons from the reviews: it's a big, busy resort that gets crowded and loud in high season, so it isn't the pick if you want pure quiet. It's best for families who want the kids to have a water park and full activities in one beachfront resort.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: With more people or two-plus kids, a Mirage Family Suite with bunk beds or a Family Residence is more comfortable and better value. Hit the water park early or late afternoon to dodge the midday sun and the crowds. And compare Agoda / Booking / Trip.com, since promo rates and family packages differ noticeably.

Na Kluea location near Terminal 21 and Lan Pho market
cons: A big resort that gets crowded and loud in high season

tags: 🌊 Opposite Pattaya beach, cross the road
entries.addr: 463/68, 463/99 Moo 9, Pattaya Sai 1 Road (Beach Road), Nong Prue, Bang Lamung
entries.storyHtml: If you want a central beachfront family hotel at a reachable price, Holiday Inn Pattaya is a name many families come back to — a 4-star IHG beachfront hotel of 531 rooms across two towers (Bay Tower for value, Executive Tower for premium), sitting on Beach Road with the sand just across the street. It scores 9.3 from 1,310 reviews. The strength families point to is the large indoor Kids Club and several swimming pools — a sea-view infinity pool and a family pool — plus a well-praised buffet breakfast. Every room in the Executive Tower has a balcony, and there's a lounge on floor 25. Honest cons from the reviews: Beach Road has traffic noise, it's a big hotel with lots of families so it's lively on weekends, and some Bay Tower rooms are starting to show their age. It's best for families who want to stay on central Pattaya beach and walk out easily for food and attractions.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: For newer rooms with a balcony in every room, choose the Executive Tower. Check IHG's "Kids Stay & Eat Free" package at booking, since kids stay and eat free in some periods under the terms. And ask for a room away from the road side if you're sensitive to traffic noise.

Opposite Pattaya beach, cross the road to the sand and seaside restaurants

cons: Beach Road has traffic noise, so ask for a room away from the road

entries.name: Somerset Pattaya
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Central Pattaya · opposite CentralFestival · walk to the beach
tags: 🍳 Kitchen rooms, good for longer stays
entries.addr: 528 Moo 10, Pattaya 2 Road, Nongprue, Bang Lamung
entries.storyHtml: If you're bringing the family for a longer stay and want a big room with a kitchen plus a place for the kids to splash in the building, Somerset Pattaya is a neat fit — a 4-star, 324-unit Ascott serviced apartment in central Pattaya, opposite CentralFestival mall, walkable to the beach. It scores 9.3 from 2,642 reviews. The thing kids love most is the pirate-themed water park on floor 24, with a pirate ship, slides and water guns, while the adults get a floor-23 rooftop infinity pool over Pattaya bay — a rare combination for a city hotel. Rooms start around 35 sqm with a kitchen, and multi-bedroom suites come with a washing machine, so it suits several nights. Honest cons from the reviews: it's pricier than a standard chain hotel in the area, and breakfast is still a work in progress. It's best for families and longer-stay travellers who want a kitchen, space and a kids' water park right by the mall.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: For a longer stay or more people, choose a studio with a kitchen or a Two-Bedroom with a washing machine to save on food and laundry. CentralFestival across the road has restaurants and a supermarket to stock the room. And take the kids up to the floor-24 water park in the afternoon to avoid the noon sun.
pros: Pirate-themed water park on floor 24 with slides and water guns, kids play all day
Rooftop infinity pool on floor 23 over Pattaya bay for the adults

cons: Pricier than a standard chain hotel in central Pattaya

entries.name: Mövenpick Siam Hotel Na Jomtien Pattaya
entries.revCount: Score 9.0 · 263 reviews · Na Jomtien beach · Accor group
entries.badge: 🌊 Lagoon slide pool · kids' club · Chocolate Hour
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Na Jomtien beach · private beachfront · ~25 min into town
entries.addr: 55 Moo 2, Sukhumvit Road KM.156.5, Na Jomtien, Sattahip
entries.storyHtml: If you want to bring the family for a quiet, private beach break but still want the full set of kids' facilities, Mövenpick Siam Hotel Na Jomtien Pattaya positions itself squarely as a beachfront family resort — a 5-star Accor property of around 262 rooms, right on Na Jomtien beach in the south. It scores 9.0 from 263 reviews. The highlight is a large winding lagoon pool with slides on the private beachfront, with a shallow corner where you can keep little ones close, plus a kids' club, a playground, family rooms with bunk beds and a babysitting service. The thing kids wait for is Chocolate Hour, a Mövenpick tradition serving free chocolate treats every afternoon, and most rooms have a sea view. Honest cons from the reviews: the location is far from central Pattaya, and dining options at some meals are more limited than you'd expect of a 5-star resort. It's best for families who want a quiet private stretch of sea with slides and a kids' club in the resort.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: With two-plus kids, a Family Sea View room with bunk beds is more comfortable and better value. Since it's far from town, keep Grab handy or drive, and plan dinner in the resort or order ahead. And don't miss Chocolate Hour in the afternoon at the Red Coral Lounge.
pros: Beachside lagoon pool with slides and a shallow corner for little ones
Kids' club, playground, family rooms with bunk beds and babysitting (from reviews)

Free Chocolate Hour every afternoon, a highlight kids love

entries.addr: 218/2-3 Moo 10, Nong Prue, Bang Lamung (by Royal Garden Plaza)
entries.storyHtml: If you want a resort with a slide pool for the kids but still right in the city, walkable to the mall and beach, AVANI Pattaya Resort fits well — a 5-star, 300-room Avani (Minor Hotels) resort in central Pattaya next to Royal Garden Plaza. It scores 9.2 from 303 reviews. What families with little ones love most is the pool with a slide, a swim-up bar, cabanas and a separate kids' pool, all set in a shady garden of mature trees that feels private and quiet even in the middle of bustling central Pattaya. Cross the road to Pattaya beach, and Walking Street is about 8 minutes' walk away; every room has a balcony. Honest cons from the reviews: the area is lively with night noise, and it's an older building — refurbished in 2016 — so some details show their age. It's best for families who want a slide pool and a leafy garden but still want a central location within walking distance of the mall and beach.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Coming as a family, choose a Family Room/Suite, which is roomy and takes kids comfortably. Ask for a garden-side or higher-floor room if you're sensitive to the night-time noise. And take the kids to the slide pool in the morning or late afternoon to avoid the harshest sun.

entries.name: Renaissance Pattaya Resort & Spa
entries.revCount: Score 9.1 · 490 reviews · Na Jomtien beach · Marriott group
entries.badge: 👶 Kids' club · kids' pool · private beach
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Na Jomtien beach · private beach · ~20–25 min into town
entries.storyHtml: If you want to bring the family for a beach break to Marriott standards — upscale but still with corners for the kids — Renaissance Pattaya Resort & Spa is a neat fit — a 5-star beachfront resort of 257 rooms and villas on the quiet, clear-water Na Jomtien beach. It scores 9.1 from 490 reviews. On the family side there's a kids' club with children's activities, a kids' pool and a Family Suite, so parents get a break while the kids have something to do, plus several outdoor beachside pools and a Beachfront Pool Villa with its own pool for families who want full privacy. It's just a few steps from the pool down to the sand. Honest cons from the reviews: the location is about 20–25 minutes from central Pattaya, resort food is pricey, and the building has been open since 2017, so there are minor details showing their age. It's best for families who want a full beach break at an upscale resort that also has a kids' club.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: With more people or if you want a private pool, look at the Family Suite or the Beachfront Pool Villa and split the cost — it works out better. Since it's far from town, arrange a car or Grab and plan your meals in the resort. And make the most of the kids' club so the adults get some downtime.

Several beachside pools, and a Beachfront Pool Villa with a private pool

entries.name: Royal Cliff Beach Hotel Pattaya
entries.revCount: Score 8.8 · 1,917 reviews · Pratamnak Hill · Royal Cliff group
entries.badge: 🎢 Funtasea kids' water park · private beach
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Pratamnak Hill · private beach on the bay · 10–15 min drive into town
entries.storyHtml: If you want a full-service beach resort with an in-house kids' water park and its own beach, Royal Cliff Beach Hotel Pattaya is a large, long-established resort on Pratamnak Hill — set on Royal Cliff Bay with a private beach that's quieter and more private than the city beaches. It scores 8.8 from 1,917 reviews. On the family side there's a Funtasea Kids World water park, a kids' pool, and the Beach Infini bay-view infinity pool, plus a games zone, spa, tennis courts, a cooking school and several styles of restaurant in one resort. Honest cons from the reviews: the resort sits up on the hill so it's inconvenient to head out, some rooms are older with their age, and there are mentions of extra charges at checkout worth clarifying in advance. It's best for families who want a private-beach resort with a water park and full activities all in one place.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: The Royal Cliff group has several buildings — choose the Royal Cliff Beach Hotel near the Beach Infini pool and the beach if swimming is the priority. Confirm any extra charges (such as service fees) at booking and before checkout. And arrange a car or Grab, since it's up on the hill and hard to walk out from.

rooms.type: Junior Suite Club Access Ocean View

tags: 🏖️ Private beach on a quiet headland
entries.storyHtml: If you want a premium family resort that's quiet and private on a headland, InterContinental Pattaya Resort fits well — a 5-star, 156-room beachfront resort in a tropical garden on the slopes of Pratamnak Hill, away from the central Pattaya bustle but just a 10–15 minute drive into town. It scores 8.9 from 567 reviews. On the family side there are three pools cascading down the slope to the sea — a main lagoon pool, a family pool and a kids' pool — plus a Kids' Club, and a quiet private beach on the headland, suiting both couples and families. There's the seaside Infiniti restaurant with sunset views, and a varied buffet breakfast at Elements with a fresh egg station. Honest cons from the reviews: the beach is smaller than in the photos, and you rely on a car to get into town. It's best for families who come to Pattaya for quiet, a private beach and a garden-resort feel rather than nightlife.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: A Junior Suite with Club Access gets lounge access and snacks through the day, which helps with food for kids and adults between activities. Put the kids in the kids' pool separate from the main lagoon pool for easier, safer supervision. And arrange a car or Grab, since it's on the headland and hard to walk out from.

entries.storyHtml: If you want a private-beach resort that's still walkable to a mall, up in North Pattaya, Dusit Thani Pattaya is a classic that has been part of the city for years — a 5-star, 457-room Dusit International resort on the headland between Pattaya Bay and Wong Amat beach, so it has private beaches on two sides that are quiet and rare in Pattaya. It scores 8.8 from 1,113 reviews. For families, the draw is the wide, botanical-garden-like tropical grounds between the rooms and the sea, a sea-view pool and kids' facilities, giving children room to run around in an oasis in the middle of a tourist city. It's at the far end of North Pattaya, a few minutes' walk to Terminal 21 mall with all its restaurants and shopping. Honest cons from the reviews: the building and some rooms are a classic structure that has seen years of use, so some rooms look dated — choose a renovated room. It's best for families who want a quiet seaside break but still want to walk to a mall.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Ask specifically for a renovated, sea-view room at booking, since it's a classic building where rooms vary by renovation round. Terminal 21 is walkable with a food court and full range of shops, handy for feeding the kids. And use the wide seaside garden to let the kids run around in the evening.

entries.storyHtml: We close the set with a budget pick families love, for anyone who wants a big room with a kitchen and bunk beds at an easy price — The Grass Serviced Suites by At Mind is a 4-star, 280-unit serviced-suite property in central Pattaya on South Pattaya Road. It scores 9.4 from 3,355 reviews, the densest review base in the set. What makes it work for families is that every room is an all-suite with a living room separate from the bedroom and a kitchenette (a big fridge, a microwave, a kettle and a dining nook), so you can cook and save on food, plus Two Bedroom Bunk Bed rooms that take several children, and there's a pool, fitness, sauna and spa. It's central, so a red truck or Grab reaches Pattaya beach and Walking Street in a few minutes. Honest cons from the reviews: it isn't on the beach, so you have to ride out, and some wings of the building are still un-renovated rooms. It's best for budget families who want space, an in-room kitchen and bunk beds for the kids.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Coming with kids, choose a Two Bedroom Bunk Bed room with bunk beds and a kitchen — roomier and better value than a single room. Ask for a renovated wing at booking for a room in good shape. And use the in-room kitchen to save on food over several nights.

The scores and highlights in this article come from reading real guest reviews on booking platforms — we didn't stay ourselves. Kids' facilities (water parks, kids' clubs, kids' pools) and kids-stay-free conditions can vary by period and package, so ask the hotel or read the details at booking. During high season (November–February), long weekends, school holidays and Songkran, prices rise and family rooms sell out fast, so book ahead. faqTitle: FAQ — questions parents ask most about family hotels in Pattaya

faq.q: ❓ Which is the best family hotel in Pattaya?
faq.a: It depends on your trip style and budget. If you want the kids to play an in-house water park all day, Centara Grand Mirage scores 9.1 with the Lost World water park and two kids' clubs on the beach. If you want to stay central and walk to the mall and beach, Holiday Inn Pattaya scores 9.3 with a large Kids Club. If you want a room with a kitchen for a longer stay, Somerset Pattaya or The Grass Serviced Suites. And if you want a quiet beach resort with a kids' club, Mövenpick Siam or Renaissance Pattaya.

faq.q: ❓ How much do family hotels in Pattaya cost?
faq.a: In this article prices start at about ฿900–6,500 per night. The most budget-friendly is The Grass Serviced Suites from ฿900 (with a kitchen); the mid-range family resorts and hotels run ฿2,400–4,800; and the premium end is InterContinental Pattaya from ฿6,500. All prices are approximate starting prices for standard rooms — family rooms and multi-bedroom suites cost more. During school holidays, high season and long weekends prices run higher than usual.

faq.q: ❓ Which Pattaya hotels have an in-house water park or slide pool?
faq.a: The clearest in-house water parks or slides are at Centara Grand Mirage (Lost World water park with a lazy river, slides and a shallow toddler zone), Royal Cliff Beach Hotel (Funtasea Kids World kids' water park), Somerset Pattaya (pirate-themed water park on floor 24), Mövenpick Siam Na Jomtien (beachside lagoon slide pool) and AVANI Pattaya (slide pool + separate kids' pool). If you mainly want the kids to swim at the hotel, these five fit best.

faq.q: ❓ Which area of Pattaya is good for families?
faq.a: North Pattaya / Na Kluea (Centara Grand Mirage, Dusit Thani) has a quieter, cleaner beach than central Pattaya and is near Terminal 21. Central Pattaya (Holiday Inn, Somerset, AVANI, The Grass) is the most walkable to the beach, malls and attractions, ideal for families who want to get around easily. Pratamnak Hill (Royal Cliff, InterContinental) is on a hillside over the bay with quiet private beaches, 10–15 minutes' drive into town. Na Jomtien (Mövenpick Siam, Renaissance) is a quiet southern zone with private beachfront, near the big southern water parks.

faq.q: ❓ What are the kid-friendly attractions in Pattaya?
faq.a: There's plenty for families around Pattaya — big water parks like Ramayana Water Park and Columbia Pictures Aquaverse, the Nong Nooch botanical garden, Underwater World Pattaya aquarium, the Sanctuary of Truth, Frost Magical Ice of Siam and Art in Paradise, plus Khao Kheow Open Zoo not far away. Most of the big water parks are in the south of the city (the Na Jomtien–Bang Saray zone), so they're easiest to reach if you stay in the southern zones.

faq.q: ❓ How far ahead should I book a Pattaya family hotel?
faq.a: During school holidays, high season (November–February), long weekends and Songkran, book 3–4 weeks ahead or more, because family rooms and bunk-bed rooms are limited and sell out fast, especially at resorts with in-house water parks. On weekdays off-season, 1–2 weeks ahead is enough. Every platform offers free cancellation, so it's worth locking in a rate like that if your plans aren't firm, then comparing Agoda / Booking / Trip.com for the best price and family package.
